content_html:
Sayyidul istighfar (the "master of seeking forgiveness") is the best wording for asking Allah's forgiveness that the Prophet ﷺ taught his Ummah, and its authentic text is in Sahih al-Bukhari (6306). He promised that whoever says it with firm belief in the morning and dies before evening, or in the evening and dies before morning, is among the people of Paradise.

In this article we give the text in al-Bukhari's wording with transliteration, explain it phrase by phrase, and cover its virtue and timing, common mistakes in its wording, and a practical plan to memorise it in five days. Then we gather the other authentic forms of istighfar (seeking forgiveness) from the Sunnah and the Quran.

What is the authentic text of Sayyid al-Istighfar?

Sayyid al-Istighfar is to say: «اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ» Allahumma anta Rabbi la ilaha illa ant, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduk, wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata't, a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't, abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayy, wa abu'u laka bidhanbi faghfir li, fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa ant. Narrated by al-Bukhari (6306). Whoever says it with certainty and dies that day or night is among the people of Paradise.

Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated the full hadith from the Prophet ﷺ:

«سَيِّدُ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ أَنْ تَقُولَ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ» «وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ النَّهَارِ مُوقِنًا بِهَا، فَمَاتَ مِنْ يَوْمِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُمْسِيَ، فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ، وَمَنْ قَالَهَا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ مُوقِنٌ بِهَا، فَمَاتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصْبِحَ، فَهُوَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الجَنَّةِ»

"The master of seeking forgiveness is that you say: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge to You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge to You my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You." He said: "Whoever says it during the day with firm belief in it and dies that day before evening, he is among the people of Paradise. And whoever says it at night with firm belief in it and dies before morning, he is among the people of Paradise." (Al-Bukhari 6306)

This hadith is among those narrated by al-Bukhari alone; Muslim did not narrate it. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in another place (6323), in the chapter on what to say in the morning, with "abu'u laka bini'matika" placed earlier and "a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't" moved to the end. The meaning is the same, and the better-known and more complete wording is that of the first narration.

Why is it called Sayyid al-Istighfar?

In Arabic, sayyid means the foremost, the one others turn to. So this is the best and most comprehensive form of istighfar. Scholars pointed out that it gathers all the meanings of repentance in two lines:

  • Tawhid: affirming that Allah is the Lord and that none deserves worship but Him.
  • Servitude: admitting that He is the Creator and that you belong to Him.
  • Keeping the covenant: holding to faith and obedience as far as you can.
  • Seeking refuge: turning to Allah from the consequences of your sins.
  • A double admission: of Allah's favour first, and then of your sin.
  • Asking and pleading: requesting forgiveness, through the fact that He alone forgives sins.

So it is not just "forgive me". It is a complete opening of praise and admission before the request, which is part of the etiquette of du'a.

What does Sayyid al-Istighfar mean, phrase by phrase?

PhraseMeaningWhat it teaches you
Allahumma anta RabbiO Allah, You are my Creator, my Owner and the Disposer of my affairsYou begin seeking forgiveness by glorifying Allah, not yourself
La ilaha illa antNone deserves worship but YouThe greatest means of drawing near to Allah is tawhid
Khalaqtani wa ana 'abdukYou brought me into being from nothing, and I belong to YouA servant returns to his Master however often he errs
Wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata'tI hold to the faith and obedience I pledged to You, and believe in Your promise of reward, as far as I canAdmitting you cannot be perfect; Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity
A'udhu bika min sharri ma sana'tI seek Your protection from the consequences and ill effects of my sinsSin has effects, and the way out of them is through Allah
Abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayyI admit and acknowledge Your favour upon meRemembering blessings before sins breaks arrogance
Wa abu'u laka bidhanbiAnd I admit my sin without excusesAdmission is the first step of repentance
Faghfir liCover my sin and pardon itThe request comes after praise and admission
Fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa antNo one has the power to forgive except YouPleading through Allah's attribute, echoing His words ﴿وَمَن يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ "and who can forgive sins except Allah?" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:135, translation: Sahih International)

The word abu'u means "I acknowledge and commit to"; in Arabic one says ba'a bihaqqihi, meaning he acknowledged his due. So the servant acknowledges two opposite things: Allah's favour upon him, and his own failure to be grateful for it. Ibn Hajar explained this in Fath al-Bari, and you will find a simple explanation in the Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths.

What is the virtue of Sayyid al-Istighfar in the morning and evening?

The virtue mentioned in the hadith is entering Paradise for whoever says it and then dies before the next period begins. It has three conditions worth understanding:

  1. "During the day" and "at night": at any part of the day or night, and it is best early on: after Fajr with the morning adhkar, and after 'Asr or Maghrib with the evening adhkar, so the virtue covers the whole day or the whole night.
  2. "With firm belief in it": believing its meanings in your heart and trusting in its reward, not repeating it with your tongue while your heart is absent. Certainty is a condition of the virtue.
  3. "He is among the people of Paradise": a great glad tiding. Scholars noted that a believer who is certain of the meanings of this dhikr will hardly persist in sin, so he is someone for whom a good ending is hoped.

That is why scholars place it at the start of the morning and evening adhkar, as in our article on the virtues of the morning and evening adhkar. If you miss it in the evening and say it at bedtime, you have still said it "at night", so add it to your adhkar before sleep if you forgot it earlier.

What are the common mistakes in the wording of Sayyid al-Istighfar?

Because the hadith is passed on by word of mouth and in images, mistakes creep in that change the wording or the meaning. The best known:

  • Dropping "laka": saying "wa abu'u bidhanbi", when al-Bukhari's wording is "wa abu'u laka bidhanbi".
  • Mispronouncing "abu'u": saying "abu" or "abuww". The correct form is "abu'u", with a hamzah (glottal stop) at the end.
  • Replacing "sana't" with "'amilt": the meaning is close, but it is better to keep the Prophet's ﷺ wording "min sharri ma sana't".
  • Dropping "mastata't" (as much as I am able): this is one of the most important parts of the hadith, because it admits that a servant cannot fulfil the covenant perfectly.
  • Mixing it with other duas: such as inserting "wabnu 'abdika ibnu amatik" (son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant), which belongs to a different du'a for worry and grief, not to Sayyid al-Istighfar.
  • Adding counts that were not narrated: the hadith sets no number, so once in the morning and once in the evening is enough. Repeating it more is fine, but do not believe the virtue is tied to a particular number.

How can I memorise Sayyid al-Istighfar in five days?

Split the hadith into five parts and learn one part each day while revising the earlier ones. Repeat the day's part after each of the five daily prayers, so you say it at least five times:

DayNew partWhat you repeat in full
1Allahumma anta Rabbi la ilaha illa antPart 1
2Khalaqtani wa ana 'abdukParts 1–2
3Wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata'tParts 1–3
4A'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't, abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayy, wa abu'u laka bidhanbiParts 1–4
5Faghfir li, fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa antThe whole hadith

Tips that help:

  • Understand before you memorise: read the table of meanings above; a phrase you understand sticks faster.
  • Notice the structure: tawhid, then servitude, then the covenant, then seeking refuge, then admitting the favour and the sin, then the request. This logical sequence keeps you from putting one phrase before another.
  • Write it out by hand once; writing fixes it in memory.
  • Teach it to your children: whoever teaches remembers more. Our article on daily adhkar for kids has methods suited to young ones.

What are the other authentic forms of istighfar?

Sayyid al-Istighfar is the best, but the Sunnah is full of other established forms that suit different moments of your day:

1. "Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh"

The Prophet ﷺ said: «وَاللهِ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً» "By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day." (Al-Bukhari 6307). And he said: «يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ تُوبُوا إِلَى اللهِ، فَإِنِّي أَتُوبُ فِي الْيَوْمِ إِلَيْهِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ» "O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day." (Muslim 2702). Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh (I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him) is the easiest form of general istighfar at any time.

2. "Rabbighfir li wa tub 'alayy"

Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: we used to count the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying a hundred times in a single sitting:

«رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ»

Rabbighfir li wa tub 'alayya innaka antat-Tawwabur-Rahim.

"My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful." (Abu Dawud 1516 and at-Tirmidhi; graded sahih by al-Albani)

3. "Astaghfirullahal-ladhi la ilaha illa huwal-Hayyul-Qayyumu wa atubu ilayh"

The Prophet ﷺ said:

«مَنْ قَالَ: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيَّ الْقَيُّومَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ، غُفِرَ لَهُ وَإِنْ كَانَ فَرَّ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ»

"Whoever says: Astaghfirullahal-ladhi la ilaha illa huwal-Hayyal-Qayyuma wa atubu ilayh (I seek the forgiveness of Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I repent to Him), he will be forgiven even if he fled from the battlefield." (Abu Dawud 1517 and at-Tirmidhi 3577; graded sahih by al-Albani)

4. The du'a of Abu Bakr in prayer

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) asked for a du'a to say in his prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ told him:

«قُلْ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي ظُلْمًا كَثِيرًا، وَلَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَغْفِرَةً مِنْ عِنْدِكَ، وَارْحَمْنِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ»

"Say: Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathira, wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa ant, faghfir li maghfiratan min 'indik, warhamni innaka antal-Ghafurur-Rahim. O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You, so grant me forgiveness from You and have mercy on me; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 834 and Muslim 2705)

Its fitting place is after the final tashahhud, before the salam.

5. Istighfar during and after the prayer

  • In ruku' (bowing) and sujud (prostration): «سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا وَبِحَمْدِكَ، اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي» Subhanaka Allahumma Rabbana wa bihamdik, Allahummaghfir li, "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 817 and Muslim 484)
  • Between the two prostrations: «رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي» Rabbighfir li, Rabbighfir li, "My Lord, forgive me; my Lord, forgive me." (Ibn Majah 897 and Abu Dawud; graded sahih by al-Albani)
  • After the salam: "Astaghfirullah" three times (Muslim 591). The details are in our article on the adhkar after salah.

6. The expiation of a gathering

«سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ»

Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik, ash-hadu an la ilaha illa ant, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.

"Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You."

Whoever says it before rising from a gathering in which there was much idle talk is forgiven what happened in that gathering. At-Tirmidhi narrated it (3433) and said: hasan sahih, and Abu Dawud narrated it too.

7. The istighfar of the prophets in the Quran

  • The du'a of Adam and Hawwa' (peace be upon them): ﴿رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers." (Surah Al-A'raf 7:23, translation: Sahih International)
  • The du'a of Yunus (peace be upon him): ﴿لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87, translation: Sahih International)

What are the fruits of istighfar in the Quran and Sunnah?

Allah says, relating the words of Nuh (peace be upon him):

﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا ﴿١٠﴾ يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا ﴿١١﴾ وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَارًا﴾

"And said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers and give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers.'" (Surah Nuh 71:10-12, translation: Sahih International)

And He says: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ "and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness" (Surah Al-Anfal 8:33, translation: Sahih International), and He praised the pious as ﴿وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ "those who seek forgiveness before dawn" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:17, translation: Sahih International). The Prophet ﷺ said: «طُوبَى لِمَنْ وَجَدَ فِي صَحِيفَتِهِ اسْتِغْفَارًا كَثِيرًا» "Glad tidings to whoever finds much istighfar in his record of deeds." (Ibn Majah 3818; graded sahih by al-Albani)

Its best time is the last part of the night before dawn, because of the hadith of Allah's descent in the last third of the night, in which He says: «مَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ» "Who will seek My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?" (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 1145 and Muslim 758)

A popular hadith on istighfar that is not authentic

The hadith "Whoever holds fast to istighfar, Allah will make for him a way out of every difficulty, relief from every worry, and will provide for him from where he does not expect" was narrated by Abu Dawud (1518), and al-Albani and others graded it weak because one of its narrators is unknown. Its meaning is sound and supported by the verses of Surah Nuh and others, but this wording should not be attributed to the Prophet ﷺ as established. See Ibn Baz's fatwa on the virtue of istighfar (Arabic).

Is istighfar with the tongue enough without repentance?

Istighfar with the tongue is an act of worship that a Muslim is rewarded for, but it is complete when the heart and actions agree with it. An-Nawawi mentioned in Riyad as-Salihin that repentance from a sin between a servant and his Lord has three conditions: to stop the sin, to regret having done it, and to resolve never to return to it. If the sin involves another person's right, there is a fourth condition: to return the right to its owner or ask his pardon. Sayyid al-Istighfar itself teaches you this: it contains admission of sin, a covenant with Allah and a request for forgiveness. What we have mentioned is a summary of scholars' views; for questions about your own situation, ask trusted scholars in your country.

Summary

The text of Sayyid al-Istighfar is in Sahih al-Bukhari (6306). Say it once in the morning and once in the evening with firm belief in its meanings, for it carries the glad tidings of Paradise for whoever dies that day or night. Memorise it in five days in parts, keep to its wording without adding or dropping anything, and add the other established forms of istighfar to your day, your prayer and your gatherings.

You will find Sayyid al-Istighfar among the morning and evening adhkar in Rafiq Al-Taa, our free Islamic app at Farhoon (Arabic interface), with a counter that remembers your place, the chapter on istighfar and repentance from Hisn al-Muslim, and a tasbih counter for general istighfar. It has no ads and needs no account, and it is coming soon to Google Play.

faq.q: How many times a day should I say Sayyidul Istighfar?
faq.a: The hadith sets no number, so it is enough to say it once in the morning and once in the evening with firm belief in its meanings, to gain the virtue in the hadith of al-Bukhari (6306). Saying it more is fine, since istighfar is good at any time, but do not believe the virtue is tied to a particular count that was not narrated.

faq.q: What does abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayya wa abu'u laka bidhanbi mean?
faq.a: Abu'u means I acknowledge and admit. The servant first acknowledges Allah's countless favours upon him, then admits his sin and shortcoming without excuses. Putting the acknowledgement of favour before the admission of sin combines gratitude with humility, and it is part of the etiquette of du'a before asking for forgiveness.

faq.q: Is Sayyidul Istighfar in Sahih Muslim?
faq.a: No. It is among the hadiths narrated by al-Bukhari alone, without Muslim. Its number in Sahih al-Bukhari is 6306, in the Book of Supplications, and al-Bukhari also narrated it as 6323 with a slight change in the order of some phrases, with the same meaning. That is why scholars place it at the start of the morning and evening adhkar.

faq.q: When do I say Sayyidul Istighfar in the morning and evening?
faq.a: With the morning adhkar after Fajr, and with the evening adhkar after 'Asr or Maghrib, because the hadith says: whoever says it during the day, and whoever says it at night. The earlier in the day or night, the longer the time the virtue covers. If you forget it in the evening, say it before sleeping, and you will have said it at night.

faq.q: Can Sayyidul Istighfar be said in the plural for a group?
faq.a: It was narrated in the singular, and it is better for each person to say it for himself in its narrated wording. Some scholars allowed an imam or someone making du'a for a group to express the meaning of istighfar in the plural in general du'a, but a narrated dhikr is kept in its wording, so say it yourself in the singular as it came.

faq.q: What is the difference between istighfar and tawbah?
faq.a: Istighfar is asking Allah for forgiveness, that is, for the sin to be covered and pardoned. Tawbah (repentance) is turning back from the sin by stopping it, regretting it and resolving not to return to it, and returning people's rights if it involved others. When both come together it is most complete, which is why the Sunnah says: Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh.
